expertise: Synthetic R7 review scope: professional decision semantics and boundary precision
Synthetic R7 review scope: AI instruction readability and semantic clarity
Synthetic R7 review scope: evidence binding and disposition lifecycle verification

ballot_rationales.rationale: Reference loading is the mechanism under review, and the selected-trigger requirement gives it a task-local decision boundary rather than a universal catalog ban.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The task-context-selection owner applies this rule only while assembling context for a single isolated agent and an immediately relevant decision.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Record excluded References and proof limits, and reopen selection when a later decision activates another Reference contract.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The loading restriction is understandable and tied to decision relevance.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: While building bounded context for an isolated task, only a Reference with a satisfied trigger that can affect the next decision is eligible for loading.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Leave speculative catalogs unloaded, identify excluded context, and state any resulting proof limitation.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The selective-load mandate is professionally valid because this Skill governs task-local context and limits Reference loading to a trigger that can change the next decision.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only during task-context selection when an individual Reference trigger changes the next decision; speculative catalog loading remains excluded.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Preserve per-Reference trigger checks, record excluded context and proof limits, and stop when required current source or task evidence is unavailable.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Benchmark definition is the mechanism, and these fields form the minimum reproducibility boundary for comparing treatment with baseline without overstating efficacy.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only to a task-local Skill efficacy benchmark making structural, empirical, routing, or regression claims.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Mark unavailable measures and caveats explicitly; do not convert missing comparison evidence into a positive efficacy claim.

ballot_rationales.rationale: These fields make a benchmark comparison reproducible and interpretable.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: When skill-efficacy-benchmark evaluates an efficacy or regression claim, each benchmark covers one task with explicit baseline, treatment, measures, verdict, caveats, and input boundary.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Classify missing comparison evidence honestly, record uncollected overhead, and keep conclusions within the demonstrated evidence class.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Each listed field is necessary to make a Skill efficacy benchmark reproducible and to prevent structural fixture results from being presented as empirical behavior evidence.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to each benchmark governed by skill-efficacy-benchmark when a baseline, treatment, or efficacy claim is being evaluated for the same bounded task.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep task, baseline, treatment, metrics, verdict, caveats, and input boundary explicit; classify missing-baseline work as structural-only with not_enough_evidence.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The one-primary count expresses a control-plane ownership invariant; supporting Layer 3 Skills and selected References remain plural and independently triggered.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when an isolated agent task context is selected under the ChangeForge layered Skill architecture.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Name all triggered supporting guidance and refresh the primary choice if task ownership materially changes.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The two singular scopes clearly define one bounded agent context.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The Registry trigger applies when one isolated agent needs task-local context and one Professional Skill must own the primary decision contract.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Create separate task contexts when ownership diverges and include only explicitly triggered supplementary Skills or References.

ballot_rationales.rationale: One primary Professional Skill is a bounded routing invariant for an isolated task, while triggered Layer 3 Skills and selected References remain independently plural.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies under the task-context-selection Registry Trigger when an isolated agent needs a minimal task-local context package.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Name exactly one primary Professional Skill, list triggered Layer 3 Skills and References separately, and route unresolved context-boundary decisions back to analysis.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The three modes yield incompatible analysis contracts, so a single selected mode is necessary to keep diagnosis, preparation, and repository answers from leaking into one another.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies after an eligible source-backed request is classified by engineering-change-analysis and before its mode contract is loaded.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Permit independently triggered supporting References while binding the dispatch and final result to one mode contract.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The three named modes are mutually exclusive analysis contracts.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: For general source-backed change preparation, verified-cause diagnosis, or a repository answer, engineering-change-analysis selects the single mode matching the request and evidence.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Issue a separate bounded dispatch if subsequent work needs another mode or output contract.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Exactly one analysis mode is required because the three supported modes have distinct triggers and output contracts, and crossing modes would make the result ambiguous.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies after engineering-change-analysis classifies the request as implementation-preparation, diagnosis-only, or source-backed-answer from current source evidence.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Bind the dispatch to the selected mode-contract, load supporting References only on their own triggers, and stop when an unresolved user decision could invalidate classification.

ballot_rationales.rationale: This sentence fixes only primary professional ownership at one; facts, supporting Skills, References, acceptance evidence, and verification remain selected by task need.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to one bounded task context for one isolated agent, not to multi-task planning or cross-agent orchestration.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Include every materially triggered support item and stop when missing source evidence prevents a reliable context boundary.

ballot_rationales.rationale: One primary Skill keeps ownership singular while allowing triggered supplements.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: For one bounded task, task-context-selection assigns one primary Professional Skill and separately names triggered Layer 3 Skills and selected References.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Split or hand off the task if no single primary decision contract remains authoritative.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The fixed primary-Skill count is valid within this capability because it defines the smallest coherent authority package for one task without limiting triggered supporting guidance.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when task-context-selection assembles current facts, authority, acceptance, verification, and stop conditions for one isolated task.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep the primary Skill singular, preserve independently triggered Layer 3 and Reference selections, refresh stale facts, and expose excluded context and residual risk.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Telemetry is a genuine required mechanism here, but the sentence limits it to cases where gateway diagnosis or operation depends on hop-level evidence.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to affected client-to-origin gateway paths whose failure or operation cannot be distinguished without correlated hop telemetry.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Collect only relevant result, duration, retry, and correlation fields while preserving proxy trust and privacy boundaries.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The telemetry requirement has an explicit operational-need condition.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: On an affected gateway path, hop-identifying telemetry is required when diagnosis or operation depends on distinguishing the reporting hop, failing hop, and upstream result.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Collect only necessary hop fields and apply privacy, retention, and bounded-cardinality controls.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Failing-hop telemetry is required only when diagnosis or operation depends on it, making the mechanism conditional on an observable gateway decision rather than universal.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to affected client-to-origin gateway paths when operational acceptance or diagnosis depends on identifying the failing hop, upstream result, duration, retries, and correlation.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Instrument only affected hops, retain correlation and upstream evidence, record proof limits, and route security, reliability, contract, or rollout concerns to their specialist gates.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Source and ownership evidence is a necessary entry condition for impact traversal, and the equivalent-inspection alternative avoids binding the rule to one tool.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies after repository-impact-inspection receives a proposed owner and change surface for a repository-specific impact question.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Return unresolved discovery to repository-context-map and label dynamic or unavailable consumers as uninspected residual risk.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The prerequisite prevents impact analysis from starting with guessed ownership.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Repository-impact-inspection begins after current source-of-truth, candidate-owner, and change-surface evidence exists from repository-context-map or equivalent direct inspection.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Stop and route discovery to repository-context-map whenever the prerequisite evidence is missing or stale.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Source-of-truth and candidate-owner evidence is a necessary entry condition for bounded impact inspection; without it, consumer and validation conclusions would lack authority.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies after a candidate owner and change surface are known through repository-context-map or equivalent current direct inspection.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Accept equivalent direct inspection, distinguish direct from inferred impact, record uninspected scope, and route missing source or ownership discovery to repository-context-map.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The mechanism token belongs to the specialist-ownership sentence, while Require governs a benefit-cost criterion; the detector joins distinct propositions and therefore misclassifies the rule family.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The service-split owner compares coupling reduction against distributed-system cost while specialist Skills retain authority over their own mechanisms.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Preserve the architectural criterion and make sentence-level detector segmentation prevent cross-proposition mechanism matches.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The word mechanisms describes retained specialist ownership, not a required mechanism.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: In the service-split role, microservice-splitting owns the integrated tradeoff and exit criteria while named specialist Skills retain authority over their respective mechanisms.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Support the coupling-versus-cost decision with current alternatives and operating evidence, and leave mechanism selection with each named specialist.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A service split is justified only when its coupling reduction exceeds the new distributed-system cost, because the Skill owns the integrated approve, reject, or defer decision.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to a proposed independently deployed service boundary after business, data, contract, failure, deployability, rollback, ownership, and operating-capacity evidence is available.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Compare viable in-process alternatives, integrate specialist-owned mechanisms, defer when evidence is insufficient, and retain phased transition, rollback, exit, and residual-owner evidence.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Review evidence is the relevant mechanism, and checking every material claim is proportionate because unsupported material claims can invalidate the downstream artifact decision.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to material claims in an ordinary pre-implementation engineering artifact within engineering-artifact-review declared scope.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Separate unverified claims, scale checking to risk, and route high-risk or release verdicts to their specialist reviewers.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Evidence for material claims is necessary to make review conclusions actionable.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: During ordinary engineering-artifact-review, claims material to the artifact decision are checked against current source or evidence from an explicit accountable owner.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Apply materiality proportionally to risk and mark unavailable evidence as unverified instead of implying certainty.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Verifying every material claim is valid for independent artifact review because downstream decisions must not rely on unsupported ownership, contract, failure, validation, or rollback assertions.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only to material claims in an ordinary Engineering Brief, Task Plan, acceptance artifact, or contract within the stated review boundary.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Use current source or explicit owner evidence, separate reviewed from unverified scope, and route high-risk design or release, deployment, and migration readiness to specialist reviewers.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Inspected evidence is conditionally required only after a control is judged inapplicable, which prevents silent omissions without forcing irrelevant controls.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies within extensibility-design when current trust, activation, compatibility, or consequence evidence makes a listed control inapplicable.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Escalate uncertain applicability and retain a concise reason tied to the inspected boundary and accountable owner.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The requirement is expressly limited to controls judged inapplicable.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: After extensibility-design evaluates the current trust, activation, and consequence boundary, any inapplicable control needs concise rationale supported by inspected evidence.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Record a control-specific non-applicability decision and apply every control whose trigger remains satisfied.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Requiring inspected evidence for an inapplicable control is valid because it prevents trust-boundary, authenticity, rollback, or recovery obligations from being dismissed without analysis.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only when an extensibility control is claimed inapplicable after evaluating artifact trust, activation mutability, consequence, isolation, compatibility, and recovery boundaries.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Record a concise non-applicability rationale with inspected evidence and escalate whenever trust, consequence, compatibility, isolation, or recovery uncertainty remains material.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Evidence before abstraction is a valid design gate because speculative extension points create compatibility and authority costs without demonstrated variation.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when extensibility-design is considering an abstraction, plugin, hook, or policy extension for claimed variation.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Use direct code or configuration until current consumers, independent change reasons, ownership, and evolution evidence are established.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The evidence categories make the anti-speculation rule directly actionable.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Before introducing an extension abstraction, extensibility-design requires current consumers, distinct change reasons, ownership, and likely evolution to demonstrate real variation.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep variation in direct code or configuration until current evidence supports a stable shared extension boundary.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Evidence of real variation before abstraction is the governing extensibility invariant and prevents speculative plugins, hooks, and compatibility surfaces from creating needless authority and lifecycle cost.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when extensibility-design evaluates a proposed extension point, plugin, policy hook, configuration variation, or other shared variation boundary.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Name current consumers, distinct change reasons, ownership, and likely evolution; prefer direct code or configuration when variation remains unproven or locally owned.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The directive mandates an impact record, not automatic test creation; that record is the Skill bounded output and must distinguish affected from uninspected surfaces.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies after the candidate owner and change surface are confirmed and repository impact is being classified.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Record existing, missing, and uninspected test surfaces without claiming that every change requires a newly created test artifact.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The instruction records test impact status; it does not mandate creating tests.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Within repository-impact-inspection, the checklist classifies affected and uninspected consumers, tests, contracts, and generated surfaces for the bounded impact map.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Record absent or uninspected test surfaces explicitly and require new tests only when acceptance or risk evidence independently justifies them.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The sentence requires recording impact status for affected and uninspected tests; it does not mandate creating, running, or retaining a test artifact as the detector family assumes.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies within repository-impact-inspection after the candidate owner and change surface are known, with tests classified as inspected impact subjects alongside consumers and contracts.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep affected and uninspected qualifiers explicit; reopen semantic review if the source later requires a test artifact rather than recording bounded impact evidence.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The two-task threshold is inherent to this product multi-task DAG boundary, and factual edges prevent graph ceremony for a single independent change.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only to an accepted source-backed Brief with at least two real tasks and genuine blocking relationships.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Emit one Task Capsule when no DAG is needed and reject placeholder nodes, cycles, or nonblocking dependency edges.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Two nodes are the minimum needed for an inter-task dependency graph.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: When an accepted Brief contains genuine multi-task dependency, integration, parallel, or release-order value, every DAG node is a real task and every edge names a blocking fact.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Return a single Task Capsule when only one task exists and never manufacture nodes to reach the threshold.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Two or more real tasks is the structural minimum for a DAG, and limiting edges to blocking facts prevents decorative dependencies and unsafe scheduling claims.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies after an accepted source-backed Brief establishes genuine multi-task work with dependencies, parallel value, integration need, or release order.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Emit a single Task Capsule when a DAG is unnecessary, validate every edge and shared resource, serialize writes in shared or unknown workspaces, and stop on unresolved scheduling boundaries.

limitations: This majority is authoring lifecycle evidence only.
It cannot satisfy readability or professional-completeness formal attestations.
The record contains no generated single-source-of-truth disposition entries.
A rewrite majority requires a source edit before any resolved governance entry can exist.
